dedupe_keys.name: fema resource typing library tool rtlt national resource typing definitions position qualifications and task books

description: The Resource Typing Library Tool is FEMA's online catalogue of national resource typing definitions, position qualifications, position task books and skillsets under the National Incident Management System. The FEMA National Integration Center maintains it, currently as version 1.9.6. Resource typing definitions describe deployable teams, equipment and facilities, from ambulance strike teams and urban search and rescue task forces to mass care, public works and incident management teams, by capability category and type level with minimum personnel, equipment and capability, so that jurisdictions can request and share resources through mutual aid consistently. Position qualifications set the training, experience and certification each role needs. Coverage is the United States, and the library is used by federal, state, local, tribal and territorial agencies. The tool is free to search and view online, and records can be exported, as a US government product. Caveats: it defines resource types, not listing actual inventories or locations, definitions are revised over time, and local typing may add unofficial types. Simulation uses: a standard vocabulary for emergency response resources in agent-based and optimisation models of mutual aid and deployment, and a basis for linking resource inventories to capability targets. Related records: NICS (platform-nics-next-generation-incident-command-system) supports incident command and OpenFEMA (data-openfema) publishes FEMA's disaster data.
